question: 84-year-old man with severe respiratory failure secondary to carcinomatous lymphangitis associated with gastric cancer. A companion of his service has begun, that same day, treatment with oral morphine 10 mg / 4 hours. The patient is restless, at 34 breaths per minute, O2 saturation is 80% with an FiO2 of 28%. What should his attitude be?

options.opa: Withdraw treatment because it may worsen respiratory failure.
options.opb: Increase the doses up to 20 mg / 4 hours according to evolution.
options.opd: Change the treatment of morphine by scopolamine.
options.ope: To add to a treatment of a risperidon.
